meta.coords: map rows/cols are 0-based tile cells of reference/tiles/shapesz/map-1-9-l<layer>.png (24x28 px); row 0 is the top of the image; the level scrolls from the bottom (high rows) upward. Pattern rows run top to bottom as in the image.
meta.enemy_method: world sim (tests/sim/worldDriver.ts, seed 1, normal, player parked at x=100) to level end; an enemy is 'on' a structure if its centre stays fixed relative to that layer's map for its whole life; cell = tile under its centre.
meta.pass_heights: layer 0 tiles 0.0, ground enemies 0.45; layer 2 tiles Background3 2.1 (rows 333-441), top enemies 2.5 (0.4 above); rows 199-324 are drawn as Background3Over (4.15) late in the level.
meta.terrain_tiles_layer2: 120-124, 130-134, 140-142, 150-152 (rock islands / boulder fill): stay on per-tile models (shapesz_bg3.py)

structures.name: fortress
structures.description: The fortress complex: a network of grey metal walkways (maze-pattern deck, rounded corners 183/184/193/194, T-junctions 181/191/192/201) framing rock islands, with the red-panel machine (160 161 / 170 171) beside the vertical walkway. Purple blocks, lava pits and craters inside it are separate patterns.
replaces_per_tile_models: walkway tiles t180 t181 t183 t184 t191 t192 t193 t194 t200 t201

inputs.note: whole complex, for reference only: too tall for one Gemini image; use -a/-b/-c (2-row overlaps) and stitch

structures.notes: Rock fill (120-124, 130-134, 140-142, 150-152) is -1 and stays on the per-tile models; purple blocks / 143 / 153 are their own patterns (-1 here). The machine cells carry enemies newsh2 15/17/53/55 (assembly-newsh2-53 'red machinery block'). An enemy (newsh2 41/131) also sits on the walkway at row 364 col 5. Walkway tile 180 also forms the bridges: minRows 2 keeps a lone walkway row from passing for either.

structures.name: bridge
structures.description: Full-width walkway bridge: a metal walkway between a rocky top rim (121) and a hanging rocky underside with roots (141), 15x3 tiles.

inputs.note: whole bridge, 4.3:1 - wider than 16:9; use -a/-b/-c (1-col overlaps), or one segment repeated

structures.notes: Rows 199-201 and 223-225 have 121 across the top; rows 236-238 join an island at the left (131 124 in cols 0-1), hence the -1s. The rims are rock-island tiles shared with plain terrain: including them in the bridge model is optional (they could stay per-tile, pattern then [[180]*15] with -1 rows). These rows are drawn in the Background3Over pass (height 4.15, over the player) once the level switches background3over (ticks ~5540-6413 in the sim).
